text.en: A recipe for 12 people uses 6 eggs and 9 cups of flour. Dividing both by the largest common number, 3, gives the simpler ratio 2 : 3. Polynomials can be simplified in the same way.

The GCD of two polynomials is the polynomial of the highest degree that divides both exactly.
To find it, factorise each polynomial and multiply the common factors, taking the smallest power of each.
The LCM is the polynomial of the lowest degree divisible by both, found by taking every factor with its highest power.
As with numbers, GCD x LCM = product of the two polynomials (up to a constant).
A rational expression is a fraction p(x)/q(x) where p and q are polynomials and q is not zero.
To simplify it, factorise numerator and denominator and cancel the common factors.
To add rational expressions, take the LCM of the denominators; to multiply, multiply numerators and denominators; to divide, multiply by the reciprocal.

why.en: Find two numbers with sum 5 and product 6.

text.en: Cancel (x + 3): the result is (x - 3)/(x + 2), where x is not -3 and not -2.

prompt.en: How do you find the GCD of two polynomials and simplify a rational expression?

requiredIdeas.en: Cancel common factors in a fraction

points.en: GCD: product of common factors with smallest powers; LCM: all factors with highest powers.
A rational expression is p(x)/q(x) with q not zero.
Simplify by factorising and cancelling common factors.
Cancel only factors, never single terms.
